title.en: Volume 177 Biographies 127: Cui Shenyou, Cui Gong, Lu Jun, Pei Xiu, Yang Shou, Wei Baoheng, Lu Yan, Xiao Houzi, Liu Zhan, Liu Zhuan, Cao Que, Bi Xian, Du Shenquan, Liu Ye, Dou Luzhan

sentences.zh: 列傳第一百三十一史憲誠史憲誠，其先出於奚虜，今爲靈武建康人。

translations.literal: Biography 131: Shi Xiancheng. Shi Xiancheng — his ancestors came from the Xi barbarians; he is now registered as a native of Jiankang in Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: [Biography 131] Shi Xiancheng. Shi Xiancheng was descended from the Xi people; his family were now registered natives of Jiankang in Lingwu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖道德，開府儀同三司、試太常卿、上柱國、懷澤郡王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daode was Grand Prefect with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, provisional Grand Minister of Ceremonies, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Prince of Huaize commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi Daode had held the titles of Grand Prefect of ceremonially equal rank to the Three Excellencies, provisional Grand Minister of Ceremonies, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Prince of Huaize.

sentences.zh: 父周洛，爲魏博軍校，事田季安，至兵馬大使、銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞、柱國、北海郡王。

translations.literal: His father Zhouluo served as a military officer of Weibo, attending Tian Ji'an, and rose to Military Affairs Commissioner, Silver-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Crown Prince's Guest, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Beihai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi Zhouluo had been a Weibo army officer under Tian Ji'an, rising to Military Affairs Commissioner, Silver-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Crown Prince's Guest, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 憲誠始以材勇，隨父歷軍中右職，兼監察御史。

translations.literal: Xiancheng at first, through talent and courage, followed his father through senior posts in the army, and also served as Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng first distinguished himself by talent and valor, following his father through senior army posts while also holding the concurrent post of Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 元和中，田弘正討李師道，令憲誠以先鋒四千人濟河，累下其城柵。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao and ordered Xiancheng to cross the river with four thousand vanguard troops, repeatedly capturing his walled camps.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, when Tian Hongzheng campaigned against Li Shidao, he sent Xiancheng across the river at the head of four thousand vanguard troops, who took one walled camp after another.

sentences.zh: 復以大軍齊進，乘勢逐北，魏之全師迫於鄆之城下。

translations.literal: Then with the main army advancing together, they seized the momentum to pursue north; Weibo's full force pressed to beneath the walls of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The main army then advanced in concert, pressing the pursuit north until Weibo's entire force had Yan city under siege.

sentences.zh: 師道窮蹙，劉悟斬首投魏軍。

translations.literal: Shidao was driven to extremity; Liu Wu beheaded him and surrendered the head to the Weibo army.
translations.idiomatic: With Shidao cornered, Liu Wu cut off his head and presented it to the Weibo forces.

sentences.zh: 錄功，超授憲誠兼中丞。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded, and Xiancheng was specially promoted to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were entered in the records, and Xiancheng was promoted out of turn to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鎮州王承宗死，弘正自魏移領鎮州。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died; Hongzheng moved from Wei to take charge of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong of Zhenzhou died, Hongzheng transferred from Wei to assume command of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 居數月，爲王廷湊所殺，遂以兵叛。

translations.literal: After several months he was killed by Wang Tingcou, who then rebelled with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was murdered by Wang Tingcou, who then rose in armed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以弘正子布爲魏博節度使，領兵討伐，俾復父冤。

translations.literal: The court appointed Hongzheng's son Bu as military governor of Weibo, to lead troops in punitive campaign and avenge his father.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Hongzheng's son Tian Bu military governor of Weibo and sent him to campaign against Tingcou so that he might avenge his father.

sentences.zh: 時幽州硃克融援助廷湊，布不能制，因自引決，軍情囂然。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Kerong of Youzhou aided Tingcou; Bu could not control the situation and took his own life, and army sentiment grew turbulent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong of Youzhou was then supporting Tingcou; unable to gain the upper hand, Bu took his own life, and the army fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 憲誠爲中軍都知兵馬使，乘亂以河朔舊事動其人心，諸軍即擁而歸魏，共立爲帥，國家因而命之。

translations.literal: Xiancheng was Central Army Commissioner for Military Affairs; seizing the disorder, he stirred their hearts with old Hebei precedents, and the armies at once rallied back to Wei and jointly installed him as commander — whereupon the state appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng, who was Central Army Commissioner for Military Affairs, exploited the chaos to appeal to old Hebei customs; the troops promptly rallied back to Wei and installed him as their leader, and the court thereupon confirmed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 時克融、廷湊並據兵爲亂，憲誠喜得旄節，雖外順朝旨，而中與硃、王爲輔車之勢，長慶二年正月也。

translations.literal: At the time Kerong and Tingcou both held troops in rebellion; Xiancheng rejoiced at receiving the commander's baton. Though outwardly he obeyed court orders, inwardly he and Zhu and Wang formed a mutual-support alliance — in the first month of the second year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: Kerong and Tingcou were both in armed rebellion at the time. Delighted to receive the commissioner's baton, Xiancheng outwardly complied with the court while secretly aligning with Zhu and Wang in mutual support — this was in the first month of Changqing 2.

sentences.zh: 尋遣司門郎中韋文恪宣慰。

translations.literal: Soon the court dispatched Wei Wenke of the Bureau of Passes as emissary to proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon sent Wei Wenke of the Bureau of Passes as an emissary to offer reassurance.

sentences.zh: 時李㝏爲亂，與憲誠書問交通。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xi was in rebellion and exchanged letters with Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi was then in rebellion and was exchanging correspondence with Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 憲誠表請與㝏節鉞，仍於黎陽艤舟，示欲渡河。

translations.literal: Xiancheng memorialized requesting a commander's baton for Xi as well, and moreover moored boats at Liyang to show intent to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng petitioned that Xi be granted a commissioner's baton as well, and moored boats at Liyang as if preparing to cross the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 及見文恪，舉止驕倨，其言甚悖。

translations.literal: When he met Wenke, his bearing was arrogant and haughty, and his words were greatly rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: When he received Wenke, his manner was arrogant and his words openly defiant.

sentences.zh: 旋聞絺爲帳下所殺，乃從改過，謂文恪曰：「憲誠蕃人，猶狗也，唯能識主。

translations.literal: Soon hearing that Xi had been killed by his own subordinates, he then changed course and said to Wenke: "Xiancheng is a barbarian, like a dog — he can only recognize his master."
translations.idiomatic: When he soon learned that Xi had been killed by his own officers, he changed his tune and told Wenke, "Xiancheng is a barbarian — no better than a dog — and knows only how to recognize his master."

sentences.zh: 雖被棒打，終不忍離。

translations.literal: Though beaten with clubs, in the end he cannot bear to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Even when beaten with clubs, he cannot bring himself to leave his master's side.

sentences.zh: 」其狡譎如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his cunning and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of his cunning and deceit.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每爲優容，尋加左僕射。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly showed him forbearance, and soon added the post of Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly indulged him, and soon promoted him to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，進秩司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Xiancheng was advanced in rank to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, Xiancheng was promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，滄景節度使李全略卒，其子同捷竊據軍城，表邀符節，舉兵伐之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe, Li Quanlue, military governor of Cangjing, died; his son Tongjie seized the army city by stealth, memorialized requesting the commander's baton, and Xiancheng raised troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 2, when Li Quanlue, military governor of Cangjing, died, his son Tongjie seized the garrison city and petitioned for the commissioner's baton; Xiancheng marched against him.

sentences.zh: 先是，憲誠與全略婚媾，及同捷叛，復潛以糧餉爲助。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiancheng had been allied by marriage with Quanlue; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly supplied grain and provisions as aid.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had earlier been connected to Quanlue by marriage; when Tongjie rebelled, he again secretly sent grain and supplies to aid him.

sentences.zh: 上屢發使申諭，尋又就加平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to admonish him, and soon additionally conferred Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent envoys to remonstrate with him, and soon afterward also named him Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 憲誠嘗遣驍將至闕下，恣爲張大，宰相韋處厚以語折剉之，憲誠不敢復與同捷爲應。

translations.literal: Xiancheng once sent fierce generals to the capital to swagger freely; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou rebuked them with words, and Xiancheng dared not again respond in concert with Tongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng once sent bold generals to the capital to boast openly; Grand Councilor Wei Chuhou rebuked them sharply, and Xiancheng dared not coordinate with Tongjie again.

sentences.zh: 時憲誠示出師共討同捷。

translations.literal: At the time Xiancheng made a show of marching out to join in attacking Tongjie.
translations.idiomatic: For a time Xiancheng made a show of taking the field jointly against Tongjie.

sentences.zh: 及滄景平，加司徒。

translations.literal: When Cangjing was pacified, he was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Cangjing was pacified, he was promoted to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 憲誠心不自安，乃遣子孝章入覲，又飛章願以所管奉命。

translations.literal: Xiancheng's heart was ill at ease; he then sent his son Xiaozhang to court for audience, and also dispatched urgent memorials offering to place his jurisdiction under court command.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy in his own mind, Xiancheng sent his son Xiaozhang to the capital for an audience and urgently petitioned to place his command under direct court authority.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 乃加侍中，移鎮河中。

translations.literal: He was then made Palace Attendant and transferred to command Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Palace Attendant and transferred to command Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 憲誠素懷向背，不能以忠誠感激其眾。

translations.literal: Xiancheng had long harbored divided loyalties and could not move his troops with sincere loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had long been of two minds toward the court and could not win his troops over with genuine loyalty.

sentences.zh: 未及出城，太和三年六月二十六日夜，爲軍眾所害，冊贈太尉。

translations.literal: Before he could leave the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month of the third year of Taihe, he was killed by the army masses; posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart the city, on the night of the twenty-sixth day of the sixth month, Taihe 3, the troops killed him; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 憲誠子 孝章孝章，幼聰悟好學。

translations.literal: Xiancheng's son Xiaozhang. Xiaozhang was clever and fond of learning from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng's son, Xiaozhang. From childhood Xiaozhang was quick-witted and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 元和中，李醞爲魏帥，取大將子弟列於軍籍。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, Li Yun was commander of Wei; he enrolled the sons of great generals on the army rolls.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign, when Li Yun commanded Wei, he enrolled the sons of senior generals on the army rolls.

sentences.zh: 孝章倡言願效文職，醞奇之，令攝府參軍。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang took the lead in declaring willingness to serve in a civil post; Yun marveled at this and ordered him to act as staff adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhang was the first to declare that he wished to serve in a civil capacity; Yun was impressed and appointed him acting staff adjutant.

sentences.zh: 及憲誠領節鉞，改士曹參軍、兼監察御史，賜緋。

translations.literal: When Xiancheng received the commander's baton, Xiaozhang was changed to Staff Section Adjutant and concurrent Investigating Censor, and granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiancheng received the commissioner's baton, Xiaozhang was made Staff Section Adjutant and concurrent Investigating Censor, with crimson robes conferred.

sentences.zh: 孝章以父在鎮多違朝旨，嘗雪涕極諫，備陳逆順之理。

translations.literal: Because his father at the command repeatedly defied court orders, Xiaozhang once wept as he remonstrated to the utmost, fully setting forth the logic of loyalty and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that his father repeatedly defied the court while in command, Xiaozhang once wept as he remonstrated with him at length on the difference between loyalty and treason.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞而嘉之，乃授檢校太子左諭德、兼侍御史，充節度副使。

translations.literal: The court heard of this and commended it, then appointed him acting Left Mentor of the Crown Prince, concurrent Attending Censor, and deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned of this, it praised his conduct and appointed him acting Left Mentor of the Crown Prince, concurrent Attending Censor, and deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷至散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，賜紫。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Regular Attendant, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Regular Attendant, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 領本道兵同平滄景，加工部尚書。

translations.literal: Leading this circuit's troops he jointly pacified Cangjing and was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Leading troops of his circuit, he helped pacify Cangjing and was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋請赴闕，文宗慰勞甚厚，憲誠亦因懇乞朝覲。

translations.literal: Soon he requested to go to court; Emperor Wenzong comforted and rewarded him very generously, and Xiancheng also earnestly begged to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: He soon requested leave to attend court; Emperor Wenzong received him with generous praise, and Xiancheng also earnestly petitioned for an audience.

sentences.zh: 上知憲誠之入覲，自孝章之謀，遂加禮部尚書，分相、衞、澶三州別爲一鎮，俾孝章領之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Xiancheng's coming to court sprang from Xiaozhang's counsel; he then added Minister of Rites, separated Xiang, Wei, and Chan prefectures into a separate command, and had Xiaozhang lead it.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Xiancheng's audience at court had come about through Xiaozhang's counsel, the emperor made him Minister of Rites, carved out Xiang, Wei, and Chan as a separate command, and placed Xiaozhang in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 孝章未到鎮，憲誠遇害。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang had not yet reached his command when Xiancheng met violent death.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xiaozhang could take up his new command, Xiancheng was killed.

sentences.zh: 上以孝章有忠節，起復爲右金吾衞將軍。

translations.literal: Because Xiaozhang had shown loyal integrity, the emperor recalled him from mourning to be General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiaozhang had shown loyal integrity, the emperor recalled him from mourning and appointed him General of the Right Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 間歲，授鄜坊節度使。

translations.literal: Within a year he was appointed military governor of Fufang.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was appointed military governor of Fufang.

sentences.zh: 居四年，遷於滑。

translations.literal: After four years he was transferred to Hua.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was transferred to Hua circuit.

sentences.zh: 一歲，入爲右領軍大將軍，改右金吾大將軍，俄授邠寧節度。

translations.literal: After one year he entered court as Grand General of the Right Leading Army, was changed to Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard, and soon received command of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: After one year he was recalled to court as Grand General of the Right Leading Army, then made Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard, and soon afterward given command of Binning.

sentences.zh: 孝章歷三鎮，雖無異績，而謹身畏法，以保初終。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang served three commands; though without outstanding achievement, he was scrupulous in person and fearful of law, thereby preserving himself from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhang held three commands. Though he won no striking distinction, he conducted himself with scrupulous regard for the law and preserved his position to the end.

sentences.zh: 開成三年十月卒，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Kaicheng he died; posthumously made Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of Kaicheng 3 and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 何進滔何進滔，靈武人也。

translations.literal: He Jintao. He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: He Jintao. He Jintao was a native of Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖孝物，祖俊，並本州軍校。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiaowu and grandfather Jun were both military officers of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather He Xiaowu and grandfather He Jun had both been army officers in their home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父默，夏州衙前兵馬使，檢校太子賓客，試太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Mo was Military Affairs Commissioner before the Xiazhou yamen, acting Crown Prince's Guest, and provisional Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His father He Mo had been Military Affairs Commissioner on the staff of Xiazhou, acting Crown Prince's Guest, and provisional Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 以進滔之貴，贈左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Because of Jintao's eminence, Mo was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Jintao rose to prominence, his father was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 進滔客寄於魏，委質軍門，事節度使田弘正。

translations.literal: Jintao sojourned as a guest in Wei, pledged himself to the army gates, and served military governor Tian Hongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jintao had come to Wei as a guest and entered military service under Tian Hongzheng, military governor of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 弘正奉詔討鄆州，破李師道，時進滔爲衙內都知兵馬使，以功授兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Hongzheng received the edict to campaign against Yanzhou and defeated Li Shidao; at the time Jintao was Yamen Inner Commissioner for Military Affairs, and for merit was made concurrent Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng campaigned against Yan at imperial order and defeated Li Shidao, Jintao was Yamen Inner Commissioner for Military Affairs and was made concurrent Attending Censor for his service.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，軍眾害史憲誠，連聲而呼曰：「得衙內都知兵馬使何端公知留後，即三軍安矣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe the army masses killed Shi Xiancheng and shouted in unison: "If we get Yamen Inner Commissioner for Military Affairs Lord He to act as acting military governor, the three armies will be at peace."
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 the troops killed Shi Xiancheng and shouted as one, "If Yamen Inner Commissioner Lord He takes charge as acting military governor, the three armies will be secure."

sentences.zh: 」推而立之。

translations.literal: " They pushed him forward and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed him forward and installed him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因授進滔左散騎常侍、魏博等州節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: The court thereupon appointed Jintao Left Regular Attendant and military commissioner for observation and disposition of Weibo and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon appointed him Left Regular Attendant and military commissioner for observation and disposition of Weibo and associated prefectures.

sentences.zh: 爲魏帥十餘年，大得民情，累官至司徒、平章事卒。

translations.literal: As commander of Wei for more than ten years, he greatly won popular sentiment; he rose in office to Minister of Education and Grand Councilor, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Wei for more than ten years and won broad popular support, rising to Minister of Education and Grand Councilor before he died.

sentences.zh: 進滔子 弘敬子弘敬襲其位。

translations.literal: Jintao's son Hongjing. Hongjing succeeded to his position.
translations.idiomatic: Jintao's son, Hongjing. Hongjing succeeded to his father's post.

sentences.zh: 朝廷時遣河中帥李執方、滄州帥劉約各遣使勸令歸闕，別俟朝旨。

translations.literal: The court at times sent Li Zhifang, commander of Hedong, and Liu Yue, commander of Cangzhou, each to dispatch envoys urging him to return to court and await separate court orders.
translations.idiomatic: The court repeatedly had Li Zhifang of Hedong and Liu Yue of Cangzhou send envoys urging him to come to court and await further imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 弘敬不從，竟就加節制。

translations.literal: Hongjing did not comply, and in the end was directly given the commander's baton.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing refused, and in the end the court simply confirmed him in the commission.

sentences.zh: 及劉稹反，不時起兵。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he did not raise troops at the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he failed to take the field promptly.

sentences.zh: 鎮州王元逵下邢、洺二州，兵次上黨，弘敬方出師壓境。

translations.literal: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou descended on Xing and Ming prefectures; his troops halted at Shangdang — only then did Hongjing march out to press the border.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuankui of Zhenzhou had already taken Xing and Ming and halted his army at Shangdang before Hongjing finally marched out to menace the border.

sentences.zh: 大中後，宣宗務其姑息，繼加官爵，亦至使相。

translations.literal: After the Dazhong era, Emperor Xuanzong pursued a policy of indulgence toward him, successively adding offices and titles until he too reached commissioner-councilor rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dazhong reign, Emperor Xuanzong pursued a conciliatory policy toward him, heaping honors upon him until he too held commissioner-councilor rank.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Xiantong reign.

sentences.zh: 子全皞嗣之。

translations.literal: His son Quanhao succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quanhao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋降符節，累官亦至同平章事。

translations.literal: The court soon bestowed the commander's baton; his accumulated offices also reached concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon conferred the commissioner's baton on him, and his accumulated honors likewise reached concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 十一年，爲軍人所害。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was killed by soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of his rule he was killed by his own troops.

sentences.zh: 子孫相繼，四十餘年。

translations.literal: Sons and grandsons succeeded one another for more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son held the command in succession for more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 韓允忠韓允忠，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Han Yunzhong. Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yunzhong. Han Yunzhong was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 舊名君雄，懿宗改賜今名。

translations.literal: His former name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong changed and bestowed his present name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Junxiong; Emperor Yizong granted him his present name.

sentences.zh: 父國昌，歷本州右職。

translations.literal: His father Guochang held senior posts in the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han Guochang had held senior posts in the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，從何弘敬破劉稹，以功爲貝州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen; for merit he was made prefect of Beizhou and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang reign he followed He Hongjing in defeating Liu Zhen and, for his service, was made prefect of Beizhou and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 以允忠故，累贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Because of Yunzhong, Guochang was repeatedly posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Yunzhong's eminence, his father was repeatedly posthumously promoted, ultimately to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 允忠少仕軍門，繼升裨校。

translations.literal: Yunzhong entered military service in youth and was promoted in succession to adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong entered army service in his youth and rose in succession to adjutant.

sentences.zh: 潞州之役，亦與其行。

translations.literal: In the Luzhou campaign he also went on the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the Luzhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 咸通十一年，何全皞爲軍眾所殺，推允忠爲帥。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xiantong, He Quanhao was killed by the army masses, and they pushed Yunzhong forward as commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 11, when He Quanhao was killed by the troops, they installed Yunzhong as their commander.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗爲普王，即降詔遙領節度，授允忠左散騎常侍、兼御史中丞，充節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was Prince of Pu; an edict was immediately issued for him to hold the command remotely, appointing Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief as acting military commissioner for observation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong was then still Prince of Pu; the court at once issued an edict confirming remote command of the circuit and appointed Yunzhong Left Regular Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief as acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 不數月，轉檢校工部尚書、魏州大都督府長史、充魏博節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was transferred to acting Minister of Works, Chief Administrator of the Weizhou Metropolitan Area Command, and military commissioner for observation of Weibo and other posts.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was made acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of the Weizhou metropolitan prefecture, and full military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 累加至檢校司空、同平章事。

translations.literal: He was successively advanced to acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to acting Minister of Works and concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 乾符元年十一月卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qianfu he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month of Qianfu 1, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 累贈太尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 允忠子 簡子簡，自允忠初授戎帥，便爲節度副使。

translations.literal: Yunzhong's son Jian. Jian, from the time Yunzhong first received command of the army, served as deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong's son, Jian. From the moment Yunzhong first received military command, Jian served as his deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，累官至檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu he had risen in office to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of the Qianfu reign he had risen to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 允忠卒，即起復爲節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: When Yunzhong died, Jian was immediately recalled from mourning to be acting military commissioner for observation.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunzhong died, Jian was immediately recalled from mourning and made acting military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 逾月，加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was made acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其後累加至侍中，封昌黎郡王。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was successively advanced to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted in succession to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Prince of Changli.

sentences.zh: 賊巢之亂，諸葛爽受其偽命河陽節度使。

translations.literal: In the turmoil of the Huang Chao bandits, Zhuge Shuang received from him the false appointment as military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao's rebellion, Zhuge Shuang accepted a bogus appointment from him as military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，寇盜蜂起，簡據有六州，甲兵強盛，竊懷僭亂之志，且欲啟其封疆，乃舉兵攻河陽，爽棄城而走。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xizong was in Shu; bandits and robbers swarmed forth. Jian held six prefectures with strong armor and troops, secretly harboring ambitions of usurpation and wishing moreover to expand his territory; he then raised troops to attack Heyang, and Shuang abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Xizong in exile in Shu and rebels rising everywhere, Jian held six prefectures and commanded a powerful army. Secretly nursing ambitions of rebellion and eager to enlarge his domain, he marched on Heyang; Shuang abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 簡遂留兵保守，因北掠邢、洺而歸，遂移軍攻鄆。

translations.literal: Jian then left troops to hold and defend, raided north through Xing and Ming and returned, then shifted his army to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian left troops to hold Heyang, raided north through Xing and Ming, then turned his army against Yan.

sentences.zh: 鄆帥曹全晸出戰，爲簡所敗，死之。

translations.literal: Cao Quanbian, commander of Yan, went out to battle and was defeated by Jian and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Quanbian, military governor of Yan, took the field and was defeated and killed by Jian.

sentences.zh: 鄆將崔君裕收合殘眾，保鄆州。

translations.literal: The Yan general Cui Junyu gathered the remnant troops and held Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan officer Cui Junyu rallied the remnant forces and held Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 簡進攻其城，半年不下，河陽復爲諸葛爽所襲。

translations.literal: Jian pressed the attack on the city; for half a year he could not take it, and Heyang was again raided by Zhuge Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian besieged the city for half a year without success, while Heyang was seized again by Zhuge Shuang.

sentences.zh: 簡因欲先討君裕，次及河陽，乃舉兵至鄆，君裕請降。

translations.literal: Jian therefore wished first to subdue Junyu, then turn to Heyang; he raised troops to Yan, and Junyu requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing first to deal with Junyu and then with Heyang, Jian marched on Yan, where Junyu offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 尋移軍復攻河陽，行及新鄕，爲爽軍逆擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Soon he shifted troops again to attack Heyang; marching as far as Xinxiang, he was struck in counterattack by Shuang's army and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He soon marched again on Heyang, but at Xinxiang Shuang's forces met him in a counterattack and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 簡單騎奔回，憂憤。

translations.literal: Jian fled back alone on horseback, aggrieved and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Jian fled back alone on horseback, sick with grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 疽發背而卒，時中和元年十一月也。

translations.literal: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died — in the eleventh month of the first year of Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: A carbuncle broke out on his back and he died, in the eleventh month of Zhonghe 1.

sentences.zh: 樂彥禎樂彥禎，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Le Yanzhen. Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Le Yanzhen. Le Yanzhen was a native of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父少寂，歷澶、博、貝三州刺史，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei prefectures and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Le Shaoji had served as prefect of Chan, Bo, and Bei and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 彥禎少爲本州軍校。

translations.literal: Yanzhen in youth was a military officer of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen entered service in his youth as an army officer in his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 韓簡之領節旄也，以彥禎爲馬歩軍都虞候，轉博州刺史。

translations.literal: When Han Jian held the commander's baton, he made Yanzhen Chief Commandant of the Horse and Foot Army and then transferred him to prefect of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jian held military command, he appointed Yanzhen Chief Commandant of the Horse and Foot Army and later made him prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 下河陽，走諸葛爽。

translations.literal: He descended on Heyang and drove Zhuge Shuang to flight.
translations.idiomatic: He took Heyang and put Zhuge Shuang to flight.

sentences.zh: 有功，遷澶州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was moved to prefect of Chan.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted to prefect of Chan.

sentences.zh: 簡再討河陽之敗也。

translations.literal: This was during Jian's second defeat in campaigning against Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: This occurred during Han Jian's second failed campaign against Heyang.

sentences.zh: 彥禎以一軍先歸，魏人遂共立之。

translations.literal: Yanzhen returned first with one army, and the people of Wei thereupon jointly installed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen was the first to return with his troops, and the men of Wei promptly installed him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 朝廷尋授檢校工部尚書，知魏博留後。

translations.literal: The court soon appointed him acting Minister of Works and acting military governor of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: The court soon appointed him acting Minister of Works and acting military governor of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 俄加戸部尚書，充節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Minister of Revenue and military commissioner for observation and disposition.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of Revenue and full military commissioner for observation and disposition.

sentences.zh: 中和四年，累加至尚書左僕射、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhonghe he was successively advanced to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhonghe 4 he was promoted in succession to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 僖宗自蜀回，加開府儀同三司，冊拜司徒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned from Shu, Yanzhen was made Grand Prefect with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned from exile in Shu, Yanzhen was made Grand Prefect of ceremonially equal rank and enfeoffed as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 彥禎志滿驕大，動多不法。

translations.literal: Yanzhen's ambitions were sated and he was arrogant; his actions were often unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Sated with success and increasingly arrogant, Yanzhen frequently acted outside the law.

sentences.zh: 一旦征六州之眾，板築羅城，約河門舊堤，周八十里，月餘而畢，人用怨咨。

translations.literal: On one occasion he conscripted the masses of the six prefectures to build a walled outer city along the old embankment at Hemen, eighty li in circumference; it was completed in a little over a month, and the people murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He once conscripted labor from all six prefectures to build an outer walled city along the old Hemen embankment, eighty li around; though finished in little more than a month, the people groaned under the burden.

sentences.zh: 彥禎子 從訓又其子從訓天資悖逆。

translations.literal: Yanzhen's son Congxun. Moreover his son Congxun was by nature rebellious and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen's son, Congxun. His son Congxun was rebellious and violent by nature.

sentences.zh: 王鐸自滑移鎮滄州，過魏郊，從訓見其女妓，利之，先伏兵於漳南高雞泊，俟鐸之至，圍而害之，掠其所有。

translations.literal: Wang Duo was transferred from Hua to command Cangzhou and passed through Wei's outskirts; Congxun saw his female entertainers and coveted them. He first hid troops at Gaojibo south of Zhang, waited for Duo to arrive, surrounded and killed him, and plundered all he possessed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Duo was transferred from Hua to Cangzhou and passed through Wei's outskirts, Congxun coveted his female entertainers, ambushed him at Gaojibo south of the Zhang River, killed him, and plundered everything he had.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷微弱，不能詰。

translations.literal: At the time the court was weak and could not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then too weak to hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 魏人素知鐸名望，議者惜之，而罪從訓。

translations.literal: The people of Wei had long known Duo's reputation; commentators lamented it and blamed Congxun.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei had long respected Duo's standing; public opinion lamented his death and condemned Congxun.

sentences.zh: 從訓又召亡命之徒五百餘輩，出入臥內，號爲「子將」，委以腹心。

translations.literal: Congxun moreover summoned more than five hundred fugitives who came and went within his sleeping quarters, styled "Son-Generals," and entrusted them with his innermost confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun also gathered more than five hundred outlaws who moved freely in and out of his private quarters, called them "Son-Generals," and entrusted them with his closest secrets.

sentences.zh: 軍人籍籍，各有異議。

translations.literal: Among the soldiers there was widespread murmuring, each with his own dissenting view.
translations.idiomatic: Dissatisfaction spread through the ranks, and many voiced objections.

sentences.zh: 從訓聞而忌之，易服遁出，止於近縣。

translations.literal: Congxun heard and grew jealous; he changed clothes and slipped away, stopping in a nearby county.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Congxun grew wary, disguised himself, slipped out of the city, and lodged in a nearby county.

sentences.zh: 彥禎因命爲六州都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yanzhen thereupon appointed him Commander-in-Chief of the six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen then appointed him supreme commander of the six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又兼相州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was also made concurrent prefect of Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was also made prefect of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 到任之後，般輦軍器，取索錢帛，使人來往，交午塗路，軍府疑貳。

translations.literal: After he took office he repeatedly transported military equipment and extorted money and silk; his envoys came and went until the roads were crowded at noon, and the army headquarters grew doubtful and divided.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he shipped arms and extorted money and silk; his agents clogged the roads, and the military headquarters grew suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 彥禎危憤而卒，眾推都將趙文㺹知留後事。

translations.literal: Yanzhen died in distress and indignation; the masses pushed forward the commandant Zhao Wenjue to handle acting military governor affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhen died, sick with fear and anger; the troops installed the commandant Zhao Wenjue as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 從訓自相州領兵三萬餘人至城下，文㺹按兵不出。

translations.literal: Congxun led more than thirty thousand troops from Xiangzhou to beneath the city walls; Wenjue held his troops and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun marched from Xiangzhou with more than thirty thousand men and halted before the city; Wenjue refused to give battle.

sentences.zh: 眾懷疑懼，復害文㺹，推羅弘信爲帥。

translations.literal: The masses were suspicious and afraid; they again killed Wenjue and pushed Luo Hongxin forward as commander.
translations.idiomatic: The troops, uneasy and afraid, killed Wenjue and installed Luo Hongxin as their commander.

sentences.zh: 弘信以兵出戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Hongxin took troops out to battle and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin took the field and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 從訓招集餘眾，次於洹水。

translations.literal: Congxun gathered the remnant troops and encamped at the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Congxun rallied his remnant forces and encamped on the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 弘信遣將程公佐領兵討擊，大敗之，梟從訓首於軍門，時文德元年春也。

translations.literal: Hongxin sent the general Cheng Gongzuo to lead troops in pursuit and attack; he inflicted a great defeat and displayed Congxun's head at the army gate — in the spring of the first year of Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin sent Cheng Gongzuo against him, routed his army, and displayed Congxun's head before the camp gate — this was in the spring of Wende 1.

sentences.zh: 羅弘信羅弘信，字德孚，魏州貴鄕人。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxin. Luo Hongxin, style Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxin. Luo Hongxin, courtesy name Defu, was a native of Guixiang in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖秀，祖珍，父讓，皆爲本州軍校。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiu, grandfather Zhen, and father Rang were all military officers of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Luo Xiu, grandfather Luo Zhen, and father Luo Rang had all been army officers in their home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘信少從戎役，歷事節度使韓簡、樂彥禎。

translations.literal: Hongxin in youth followed military service and successively served military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin entered military service in his youth and served under the military governors Han Jian and Le Yanzhen.

sentences.zh: 光啟末，彥禎子從訓忌牙軍，出居於外，軍眾廢彥禎，推趙文㺹權主軍州事。

translations.literal: At the end of Guangqi, Yanzhen's son Congxun feared the yazi troops and went to live outside the city; the army masses deposed Yanzhen and pushed Zhao Wenjue to provisionally direct army and prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Guangqi reign, Congxun, fearing the yazi troops, moved outside the city; the army deposed Yanzhen and installed Zhao Wenjue to govern the circuit provisionally.

sentences.zh: 眾復以爲不便，因推弘信爲帥。

translations.literal: The masses again found this unsuitable and therefore pushed Hongxin forward as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Finding this arrangement unsatisfactory, the troops then installed Hongxin as commander.

sentences.zh: 先是，有鄰人密謂弘信曰：「某嘗夜遇一白鬚翁，相告雲，君當爲土地主。

translations.literal: Earlier, a neighbor had secretly told Hongxin: "I once met a white-bearded old man at night who told me you are to become lord of the land."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a neighbor had told him in secret, "I once met a white-bearded old man at night who said you would become lord of this land."

sentences.zh: 如是者再三。

translations.literal: This happened again and again.
translations.idiomatic: He said this had happened again and again.

sentences.zh: 」弘信竊異之。

translations.literal: " Hongxin privately marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin had privately wondered at the omen.

sentences.zh: 及廢文㺹，軍人聚呼曰：「孰願爲節度使者？

translations.literal: When Wenjue was deposed, the soldiers gathered and shouted: "Who wishes to be military commissioner?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wenjue was removed, the soldiers called out together, "Who will be military commissioner?"

sentences.zh: 」弘信即應之曰：「白鬚翁早以命我。

translations.literal: " Hongxin at once answered: "The white-bearded old man long ago commanded me."
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin answered at once, "The white-bearded old man long ago destined me for it."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃環而視之，曰：「可也。

translations.literal: " The masses then encircled and looked at him, saying: "He will do."
translations.idiomatic: The men surrounded him and said, "He will do."

sentences.zh: 」由是立之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they installed him.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis they installed him.

sentences.zh: 僖宗聞之，文德元年四月，詔加工部尚書，權知節度留後。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong heard of it, in the fourth month of the first year of Wende an edict added Minister of Works and acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong learned of this, in the fourth month of Wende 1 he was ordered to serve as Minister of Works and acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 七月，復加金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書右僕射，充魏博節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was further made Golden-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and military commissioner for observation and disposition of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was further made Golden-Gleam Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Right Vice Director, and full military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 龍紀中，加檢校司空、同平章事，封豫章郡公。

translations.literal: In the Longji era he was made acting Minister of Works, concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longji reign he was made acting Minister of Works, concurrent Grand Councilor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，朱全忠急攻兗鄆，朱瑄求援於太原。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era Zhu Quanzhong pressed the attack on Yan and Yanzhou; Zhu Xuan sought aid from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning reign Zhu Quanzhong pressed hard against Yan and Yanzhou, and Zhu Xuan sought help from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太原發軍，假道於魏，令大將李存信屯莘縣。

translations.literal: Taiyuan dispatched troops, asking passage through Wei, and ordered the great general Li Cunxin to encamp at Shen county.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan sent an army through Wei by permission and stationed the general Li Cunxin at Shen county.

sentences.zh: 存信御軍無法，侵魏之芻牧，弘信不平之。

translations.literal: Cunxin commanded the army without discipline and encroached on Wei's fodder and pastures; Hongxin was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxin disciplined his troops poorly and seized Wei's fodder and pasturelands, which angered Hongxin.

sentences.zh: 全忠復遣人謂之曰：「太原志吞河朔，回戈之日，貴道堪憂。

translations.literal: Quanzhong again sent someone to tell him: "Taiyuan intends to swallow Hebei; on the day they turn their spears back, your honored circuit will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent word again: "Taiyuan means to swallow Hebei; when they turn homeward, your circuit will be in grave danger."

sentences.zh: 」弘信乃托好於汴，出師三萬攻存信，敗之。

translations.literal: " Hongxin thereupon professed friendship with Bian and marched out thirty thousand to attack Cunxin and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin therefore professed friendship with Bian, marched out thirty thousand men against Cunxin, and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 太原怒，舉兵攻魏，營於觀音門外。

translations.literal: Taiyuan was enraged and raised troops to attack Wei, encamping outside the Guanyin Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Taiyuan attacked Wei and encamped outside the Guanyin Gate.

sentences.zh: 汴將葛從周援之，屯於洹水。

translations.literal: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to his aid and encamped at the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Ge Congzhou came to his aid and encamped on the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 李克用子落落時爲鐵林軍使，爲從周所擒，乃退歸。

translations.literal: Li Keyong's son Luoluo was then Iron Forest Army commander; he was captured by Congzhou, and they then withdrew and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong's son Luoluo, then commander of the Iron Forest Army, was captured by Congzhou, and the Taiyuan forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是太原之師，每歲侵擾相、魏，魏人患之。

translations.literal: From this time the Taiyuan army every year raided Xiang and Wei, and the people of Wei were afflicted by it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Taiyuan raided Xiang and Wei year after year, to the great distress of the Wei command.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠方事兗鄆，懼弘信離貳，每歲時賂遺，必卑辭厚禮答貺。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong was then engaged with Yan and Yanzhou and feared Hongxin might turn aside; every year at the seasons he sent gifts, and Hongxin always answered with humble words and generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: While Quanzhong was campaigning in Yan and Yanzhou, he feared Hongxin might turn against him and every year sent lavish seasonal gifts, which Hongxin always answered with humble words and generous courtesy.

sentences.zh: 全忠對魏使北面拜而受之，曰：「六兄比予倍年已上，兄弟之國，安得以常鄰遇之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong toward Wei's envoy bowed facing north to receive them, saying: "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my years; between brother states, how can one treat them as ordinary neighbors?"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong would bow northward to receive Wei's envoys and say, "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my age; between brother states, how can one treat a neighbor as an ordinary acquaintance?"

sentences.zh: 」弘信以爲厚己，亦推心焉。

translations.literal: " Hongxin took this as honoring himself and also gave his heart in return.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin took this as deep respect for himself and gave Quanzhong his full trust in return.

sentences.zh: 弘信累官至檢校太師、守侍中、臨清王。

translations.literal: Hongxin rose in office to acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin rose to acting Grand Preceptor, Guardian Palace Attendant, and Prince of Linqing.

sentences.zh: 光化元年九月卒，年六十三，贈太師，追封北平王，謚曰莊肅。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Guanghua he died, aged sixty-three; posthumously made Grand Preceptor, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Northern Peace, posthumous title Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Guanghua 1, at the age of sixty-three; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Northern Peace, and given the posthumous title Zhuangsu.

sentences.zh: 子威。

translations.literal: His son Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wei.

sentences.zh: 弘信子 威威，字端己。

translations.literal: Hongxin's son Wei. Wei, style Duanji.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin's son, Wei. Wei, courtesy name Duanji.

sentences.zh: 文德初，授左散騎常侍，充天雄軍節度副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wende he was appointed Left Regular Attendant and deputy military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wende reign he was appointed Left Regular Attendant and deputy military commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 自龍紀至乾寧，十年之中，累加官爵。

translations.literal: From Longji to Qianning, within ten years he was successively advanced in offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: From the Longji through the Qianning reigns, over ten years he accumulated honors and titles.

sentences.zh: 弘信卒，襲父位爲留後，朝廷從而命之。

translations.literal: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded to his father's post as acting military governor, and the court thereupon appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxin died, Wei succeeded him as acting military governor, and the court confirmed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 天復末，累加至檢校太傅、兼侍中、長沙王。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianfu he was successively advanced to acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Tianfu reign he had risen to acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Palace Attendant, and Prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 天祐初，授檢校太尉、守侍中，進封鄴王，賜號「忠勤宣力致理功臣」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he was appointed acting Grand Commandant, Guardian Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the title "Meritorious Minister Who Is Loyal, Diligent, Expands Power, and Brings Order."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianyou reign he was made acting Grand Commandant and Guardian Palace Attendant, advanced to Prince of Ye, and granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Diligence Who Expands Power and Brings Order.

sentences.zh: 魏之牙中軍者，自至德中，田承嗣盜據相、魏、澶、博、衞、貝等六州，召募軍中子弟置之部下，遂以爲號。

translations.literal: Wei's yazi central army: from the Zhide era Tian Chengsi seized by stealth Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei and the other six prefectures, recruited sons of army families and placed them under his command, and thus they took this as their name.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's yazi central army dated from the Zhide era, when Tian Chengsi seized the six prefectures of Xiang, Wei, Chan, Bo, Wei, and Bei, enrolled sons of army families under his command, and gave them this name.

sentences.zh: 皆豐給厚賜，不勝驕寵。

translations.literal: All received rich provisions and generous rewards, beyond bearing in pride and favor.
translations.idiomatic: They were lavishly paid and richly rewarded until pride and indulgence knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 年代浸遠，父子相襲，親黨膠固。

translations.literal: As the years gradually lengthened, father and son succeeded one another and kin and partisans bonded solid.
translations.idiomatic: Over the generations father succeeded son, and kin and allies grew ever more tightly bound.

sentences.zh: 其凶戾者，強買豪奪，逾法犯令，長吏不能禁。

translations.literal: The violent among them forcibly bought and seized by main force, transgressed law and violated orders, and senior officials could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The most brutal among them seized property by force, broke the law with impunity, and local officials could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 變易主帥，有同兒戲，如史憲誠、何進滔、韓君雄、樂彥禎，皆爲其所立。

translations.literal: Changing commanders was like child's play; such men as Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen were all installed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing commanders was child's play to them; Shi Xiancheng, He Jintao, Han Junxiong, and Le Yanzhen had all been installed by the yazi.

sentences.zh: 優獎小不如意，則舉族被害。

translations.literal: If rewards and favors fell slightly short of their wishes, whole clans were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: If rewards fell even slightly short of their expectations, entire clans were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 威懲其往弊，雖以貨賂姑息，而心銜之。

translations.literal: Wei punished their past abuses; though he used bribes to appease them, in his heart he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wei set himself to curb their abuses; though he bought them off with gifts, he nursed deep resentment against them.

sentences.zh: 威嗣世之明年，正月，幽州劉仁恭擁兵十萬，謀亂河朔，進陷貝州，長驅攻魏。

translations.literal: In the year after Wei succeeded to the hereditary post, in the first month, Liu Rengong of Youzhou mustered one hundred thousand troops, plotted disorder in Hebei, advanced and seized Bei prefecture, and drove straight to attack Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the year following Wei's succession, Liu Rengong of Youzhou mustered one hundred thousand men, plotted to throw Hebei into chaos, took Bei prefecture, and marched straight on Wei.

sentences.zh: 威求援於汴。

translations.literal: Wei sought aid from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sought help from Bian.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣將李思安屯於洹水。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent the general Li Si'an to encamp at the Huan River.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to encamp on the Huan River.

sentences.zh: 葛從周自邢、洺引軍入魏。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou led troops from Xing and Ming into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou led his army from Xing and Ming into Wei.

sentences.zh: 燕將劉守文、單可及攻汴軍於內黃。

translations.literal: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keyi attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan generals Liu Shouwen and Shan Keyi attacked the Bian army at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 思安逆戰，大敗之，乘勝追躡。

translations.literal: Si'an met them in battle and inflicted a great defeat, then pressed the victory in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Si'an met them in battle, routed them, and pressed the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 從周出會掩擊，覆敗燕軍，斬首三萬。

translations.literal: Congzhou came out to join in a concealed strike and utterly defeated the Yan army, beheading thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou joined the attack from another direction, crushed the Yan army, and took thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 三年，威引汴軍攻滄州以報之。

translations.literal: In the third year Wei led Bian troops to attack Cangzhou in reprisal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Wei led Bian troops against Cangzhou in reprisal.

sentences.zh: 自是，威感全忠援助之恩，合從景附。

translations.literal: From this time Wei was moved by gratitude for Quanzhong's aid and joined in alliance and close attachment.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Wei, grateful for Quanzhong's aid, entered into close alliance with him.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年七月十三日夜，牙軍裨校李公佺作亂，威僅以身免。

translations.literal: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month of the second year of Tianyou, the yazi army adjutant Li Gongquan rebelled; Wei barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the thirteenth day of the seventh month, Tianyou 2, the yazi adjutant Li Gongquan rebelled, and Wei barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 公佺出奔滄州。

translations.literal: Gongquan fled to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gongquan fled to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 自是愈懼，遣使求援於全忠，密謀破之。

translations.literal: From this he grew ever more fearful, sent envoys to seek aid from Quanzhong, and secretly plotted to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter ever more afraid, he sent envoys to Quanzhong for aid and secretly plotted their destruction.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣李思安會魏博軍，再攻滄州。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an to join with Weibo troops and again attack Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Li Si'an with Weibo troops to attack Cangzhou again.

sentences.zh: 全忠女妻威子廷規，先是卒。

translations.literal: Quanzhong's daughter had married Wei's son Tinggui; she had died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong's daughter had been married to Wei's son Tinggui, who had died earlier.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣長直軍校馬嗣勳選兵千人，密於輿中實兵甲入魏，言助女葬事。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent the long-service army officer Ma Sixun to select one thousand troops, secretly filling palanquins with armor and weapons to enter Wei, saying they came to assist with the daughter's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent the veteran officer Ma Sixun with a thousand picked men, arms hidden in funeral litters, on the pretext of assisting with his daughter's burial.

sentences.zh: 三年正月五日，嗣勳至，全忠親率大軍濟河，言視行營於滄景。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Sixun arrived; Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, saying he was going to inspect the camps at Cangjing.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the first month of the third year Sixun arrived; Quanzhong personally led a great army across the river, claiming he was going to inspect the Cangjing front.

sentences.zh: 威欲因而出迎，至期，即假全忠帳下銳卒入而夾攻之。

translations.literal: Wei wished to take the occasion to go out to welcome him; when the day came, he would borrow Quanzhong's crack troops from his staff to enter and attack them from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Wei planned to go out to welcome him and, when the day came, use Quanzhong's crack troops to enter the city and attack the yazi from within and without.

sentences.zh: 牙軍頗疑，堅請不出。

translations.literal: The yazi army was quite suspicious and firmly begged that he not go out.
translations.idiomatic: The yazi grew suspicious and firmly urged him not to leave the city.

sentences.zh: 威恐洩其事，慰納之。

translations.literal: Wei feared the affair would leak and comforted and appeased them.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his plot would leak out, Wei reassured them.

sentences.zh: 是月十四日夜，率廝養百十輩，與嗣勳合攻之。

translations.literal: On the night of the fourteenth day of that month he led a hundred-odd personal attendants and joined Sixun in a combined attack.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the fourteenth he led a little more than a hundred personal retainers and joined Sixun in the assault.

sentences.zh: 時宿於牙城者千人，遲明殺之殆盡；

translations.literal: At the time a thousand were quartered in the yazi city; by dawn they were killed nearly to the last man;
translations.idiomatic: About a thousand yazi were quartered in the inner city; by dawn nearly all had been killed;

sentences.zh: 凡八千家，皆破其族。

translations.literal: in all eight thousand households — all their clans were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: eight thousand households in all had their entire clans destroyed.

sentences.zh: 魏軍攻滄州者，在歷亭聞有變，其將史仁遇擁之，保於高唐。

translations.literal: The Wei troops attacking Cangzhou, at Liting heard there was a disturbance; their general Shi Renyu rallied them and held Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei troops besieging Cangzhou, hearing of the upheaval at Liting, were rallied by their general Shi Renyu, who held Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 六州之內，皆爲讎敵，累月平之。

translations.literal: Within the six prefectures all became enemies; it took months to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the six prefectures they were hunted as enemies, and months passed before order was restored.

sentences.zh: 威仕梁數年後卒，年三十四，位至守太師、兼中書令，贈尚書令，謚曰貞壯。

translations.literal: After serving Liang several years Wei died, aged thirty-four, having reached Guardian Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat, posthumous title Zhenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in Liang service Wei died at thirty-four, having reached Guardian Grand Preceptor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat; he was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Zhenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 威性明敏，達於吏道。

translations.literal: Wei's nature was bright and keen; he was accomplished in the ways of administration.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was quick-witted and thoroughly versed in administration.

sentences.zh: 伏膺儒術，招納文人，聚書至萬卷。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to Confucian learning, recruited literary men, and amassed books to ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to Confucian learning, gathered scholars about him, and collected ten thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 每花朝月夕，與賓佐賦詠，甚有情致。

translations.literal: On every flower-bright morning and moonlit evening he composed and recited poetry with his guests and staff, with much charm and feeling.
translations.idiomatic: On spring mornings and moonlit evenings he would compose and recite poetry with his guests and staff, with real grace and feeling.

sentences.zh: 錢塘人羅隱者，有當世詩名，自號「江東生」。

translations.literal: There was Luo Yin of Qiantang, who had poetic fame in his age and styled himself "Born East of the River."
translations.idiomatic: There was Luo Yin of Qiantang, a poet of contemporary renown who styled himself "Born East of the River."

sentences.zh: 威遣使賂遺，敘其宗姓，推爲叔父。

translations.literal: Wei sent envoys with gifts, recounted their shared clan surname, and honored him as paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent envoys with gifts, traced their shared clan name, and treated him as an uncle.

sentences.zh: 隱亦集其詩寄之。

translations.literal: Yin also gathered his poems and sent them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yin in turn assembled his poems and sent them to Wei.

sentences.zh: 威酷嗜其作，目己所爲曰《偷江東集》，凡五卷，今鄴中人士諷詠之。

translations.literal: Wei was passionately fond of his writings and titled his own compositions Collected Poems Pilfered from East of the River, five scrolls in all; today the people of Ye recite and chant them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was devoted to Yin's work and titled his own compositions Collected Poems Pilfered from East of the River in five scrolls; people in Ye still recite them today.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：魏、鎮、燕三鎮，不能制之也久矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: The historian says: The three commands of Wei, Zhen, and Yan — the court has long been unable to control them.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The commands of Wei, Zhen, and Yan have long defied central control.

sentences.zh: 兵強地廣，合從連衡。

translations.literal: Their troops are strong and their lands broad; they ally in vertical leagues and horizontal covenants.
translations.idiomatic: Their armies are strong and their territories vast; they league together in shifting alliances.

sentences.zh: 爵命雖假於朝廷，群臣自謀於元帥。

translations.literal: Though titles and commissions are borrowed from the court, the ministers plot among themselves under their commanders-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Though their titles come from the court on loan, their officers plot among themselves under their commanders.

sentences.zh: 如史憲誠等五家，其初皆因此而得之，其後亦因此而失之。

translations.literal: Such five houses as Shi Xiancheng's — at first they all gained power thereby, and later they lost it thereby as well.
translations.idiomatic: The five houses represented here, beginning with Shi Xiancheng, first won power in this way and later lost it by the same means.

sentences.zh: 蓋不知取之以權，守之以仁，則遠矣。

translations.literal: For they did not know that to take power by expedient authority and to keep it by humane virtue is a path far removed from theirs.
translations.idiomatic: They did not understand that power seized by expedient means must be held by humane governance — a lesson far beyond them.

sentences.zh: 若善繼者，史氏、羅氏之二子有焉，其餘不足觀也。

translations.literal: Among those who succeeded well, the two sons of the Shi and Luo houses qualify; the rest are not worth regarding.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who ruled well, only the sons of the Shi and Luo houses merit notice; the rest are scarcely worth mention.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：逆取順守，古亦有之。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The encomium says: To seize by rebellion and to keep by obedience — antiquity too had such cases.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Seizing power by force yet holding it through loyal service — history offers precedents even for that.

sentences.zh: 如其逆守，滅亡必隨。

translations.literal: If one keeps power by rebellion, destruction and extinction must follow.
translations.idiomatic: But to hold power through continued rebellion is to invite certain ruin.

sentences.zh: 史、何、韓、樂，世數盛衰。

translations.literal: Shi, He, Han, and Le — generation after generation, rise and fall.
translations.idiomatic: The houses of Shi, He, Han, and Le rose and fell across the generations.

sentences.zh: 足以爲鑒，念茲在茲。

translations.literal: They are sufficient to serve as a mirror; let this be kept ever in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Their story is warning enough — let it be kept always in mind.
